result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.mixing_expansion()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get the mixing expansion of a set of nodes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L41709-L41769){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.mixing_expansion( S, T=None, weighted=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Mixing expansion](/assets/graphs/mixing-expansion.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same graph and set S. Three of its ten edges cross the cut (accent), so 3 of the 20 edge ends in the graph lie on the cut: mixing expansion 3 / 20 = 0.15." width="100%"} Mixing expansion is the cut size divided by twice the number of edges in the graph: `cut / (2m)`, the share of all edge ends that sit on cut edges. It compares a cut with the size of the whole network rather than with the set, which makes it a natural measure when the cut is meant to be a small fraction of all connections (for example, how much traffic crosses between two regions). `T` defaults to the complement of `S`. As in NetworkX, the denominator counts edges, even when the cut uses weights. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [S]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : One set of nodes, as integer IDs or string labels. [T]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : The other set. If `None` (default), all nodes not in `S`. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights in the cut. If `None` (default), follows the graph. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The mixing expansion. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `S=` is empty, a node does not exist, or the graph has no edges. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} One of seven edges crosses between the triangles, so 1 / 14 of all edge ends lie on the cut: ::: {#cb54f428 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E"), ("E", "F"), ("F", "D")]) ) graph.mixing_expansion(["A", "B", "C"]) == 1 / 14 ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` True ``` ::: :::
